heroHeadline: Balikatan 2026 Day 15: PH-US-Japan CLLFX-N Live Fire at Ilocos Norte as Sandy Cay 1 Opens New SCS Front — Atin Ito Plants Philippine Flag, China Accuses 'Illegal Landing', 4 PRC Research Vessels Threatened with Expulsion; ASEAN Summit Opens May 7
heroSubtitle: On May 4, 2026 (Balikatan Day 15), Philippine, US, and Japanese forces executed the Counter-Landing Live Fire Exercise North (CLLFX-N) at La Paz Sand Dunes in Laoag, Ilocos Norte — the northernmost Luzon exercise of the entire Balikatan 2026 programme — deploying HIMARS rocket systems, Apache Longbow attack helicopters, and 105mm howitzers in a simulated defense of Northern Luzon's coastline against mock amphibious invasion, directly covering the Luzon Strait approach between the Philippines and Taiwan. A day earlier, on May 3, Filipino civilian coalition Atin Ito sailed overnight and planted the Philippine national flag on Sandy Cay 1 in the Spratly Islands at dawn, triggering an immediate exchange of accusations: China's Coast Guard accused five Philippine nationals of 'illegal landing,' while the Philippines National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea identified four Chinese vessels conducting what it called 'illegal research' at the feature and threatened to deploy aircraft and ships for expulsion. Sandy Cay 1 is approximately 160 nautical miles from Palawan — well within the Philippines' EEZ — and is part of the Kalayaan Island Group administered under Marcos Executive Order 111 (March 2026). The confrontation opened a new territorial flash point alongside BRP Sierra Madre (Second Thomas Shoal), Scarborough Shoal's floating barriers, and the PLA STC's three-axis counter-posture during Balikatan (Scarborough, east Luzon, Luzon Strait). On May 1, the UK House of Commons Defence Committee published its year-long AUKUS inquiry, warning that funding shortfalls risk delays to the SSN-AUKUS submarine class — a concern amplified by Australia's April 23 announcement of a 34% near-term cost increase. Balikatan 2026 closes May 8; the 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit opens in Cebu on May 7 with the South China Sea Code of Conduct as the centerpiece agenda item, three days after China analyst Wu Shicun called final agreement '100 per cent not likely' in 2026.
